general: Extract every entity of the supplied types. Return exact spans from the query. Leave other text unlabelled.
C1 Words for a nationality, people or language, such as "American", "British", "Polish" or "Russian", are never Country or Location; label them Other.

classes.name: Country
rules: CO1 Examples: "U.S.", "India", "China", "Germany", "United States".

classes.name: Election
classes.description: Refers to an organized process in which individuals vote to choose a candidate or make a decision.
rules: EL1 If an event mentioned in the text pertains to an election, annotate it as an election entity.

EL2 An Election span starts at its year, or at the month when one comes before the year, and covers the whole name: "1997 Canadian federal election", "1977 Ontario general election", "2016 Basque regional election", "February 1974 United Kingdom general election". Never label the country or region inside it on its own.

EL3 Examples: "1997 Irish general election", "1992 United States presidential election", "1920 United States presidential election", "2000 United States presidential election", "2008 United States presidential election".

classes.name: Organization
classes.description: Refers to a structured group, institution, company, or association that is not a political party.
rules: OR1 International federations of parties are Organization, not PoliticalParty: "Liberal International".
OR2 Examples: "NARAL Pro-Choice America", "Planned Parenthood", "National Right to Life Committee", "United Daughters of the Confederacy", "Sons of Confederate Veterans".

classes.name: Politician
classes.description: Refers to a person who is actively engaged in politics, holding a public office, involved in political activities or part of a political party.
rules: PO1 If a person entity is identified as a politician, annotate that person's name as a politician entity.

PO2 Candidates, party leaders and party officials are Politician even if they never held office, also when named by surname only: "Nicole Malliotakis", "Guy Millner", "Giacomo Montalto", "Samis", "Dubé".
PO3 Examples: "Bush", "Ronald Reagan", "Al Gore", "Joseph Stalin", "Richard Nixon".

classes.name: PoliticalParty
classes.description: A political party is an organization that coordinates candidates to compete in a particular country's elections.
rules: PP1 Also annotate acronyms of political parties.
PP2 Groups that run in elections are PoliticalParty even without the word Party in their name: "Euskadiko Ezkerra", "Polisario Front", "Kuomintang", "Fatah", "GroenLinks".
PP3 Examples: "SPD", "National Party of Australia", "Sinn Féin", "FDP", "Liberal Party of Australia".

classes.name: Location
classes.description: Refers to a specific geographical or structural location.
rules: LO1 This includes but is not limited to: places (e.g., parks, landmarks), bridges, cities, towns, villages, areas and other distinct regions.
LO2 Examples: "Paris", "London", "Berlin", "Rome", "Dublin".

classes.name: Person
classes.description: Refers to an individual's name that is not a politician.
rules: PE1 Person is only for people with no political role, such as actors, singers, writers, journalists and scholars.
PE2 Examples: "Bennelong", "Zappa", "Tower", "Andrea Fischer", "Wyden".

classes.name: Other
classes.description: Refers to named entities that are not included in any other category.
rules: OT1 A party word used alone for a person, voter or adjective is Other, not PoliticalParty: "Republican", "Democrat", "Republicans", "Democrats".
OT2 Examples: "Republican", "German", "Democrat", "Soviet", "Republicans".

classes.name: Event
classes.description: Refers to a significant occurrence or happening.
rules: EV1 Such as wars, conferences, summits, conventions, etc.
EV2 Examples: "Decembrist revolt", "1952 Republican National Convention", "1943 Tehran Conference", "World War II", "1983 Commonwealth heads of Government summit".
